h: לְעֶרֶב יוֹם הַכִּפּוּרִים, ז׳ Erev Yom Kippur, 7

p: "And who will say that it was a man,
and not the Holy One, blessed be He, in His glory,
who would enter and go out with him?"
"And the Kohen Gadol was not a man,
בְּשָׁעָה שֶׁהָיָה רוּחַ הַקֹּדֶשׁ שׁוֹרָה עָלָיו
at the time that ruach hakodesh rested upon him,
his face would burn like torches;
כִּי שִׂפְתֵי כֹהֵן יִשְׁמְרוּ דַעַת וְגוֹמֵר
'For the lips of the kohen shall guard knowledge,' etc.,
'for he is a messenger of Hashem of Hosts'
The Matnos Kehunah already raised the difficulty:
that it was the Holy One, blessed be He, in His glory,
in order to resolve what is written,
in line with the exposition of the Yerushalmi (Yoma 5:2):
"even those of whom it is written,
'And the likeness of their faces was the face of a man'"
and afterward he concludes on his question:
"And the Kohen Gadol was not a man,"
meaning that he was an angel —
so the difficulty returns to its place.
He wrote that Rabbi Abahu retracted
and explained "and no man" according to its plain meaning.
But it is difficult to say of Rabbi Abahu,
that the Kohen Gadol, upon entering the Kodesh HaKodashim,
for there was a stripping away of physicality,
and he was only a soul —
נֵר ה׳ נִשְׁמַת אָדָם (מִשְׁלֵי כ, כז).
"The soul of man is the lamp of Hashem" (Mishlei 20:27).
was the root of Torah she'b'al peh,
דִּכְתִיב: כִּי שִׂפְתֵי כֹהֵן יִשְׁמְרוּ דַעַת
as it is written, "For the lips of the kohen shall guard knowledge,
and they shall seek Torah from his mouth";
and this is "the mouth of Hashem,"
as stated in the holy Zohar
there ascended the mouth that rules over all,
that on Shabbos the mouth in the soul was created.
Now certainly the mouth was created
on Erev Shabbos with Hashem Yisbarach
and this was created on Shabbos,
as stated in the holy Zohar
"'And Elokim finished on the seventh day'
And on Shabbos, which is the day of souls,
a person is then able to speak words
that will be the words of the living God,
and this is called "the mouth of Hashem."
And Hashem Yisbarach dwells in the heart,
that the Holy One, blessed be He, is called
As it is written, 'Rock of my heart
and my portion is Elokim forever'
And the mouth is the messenger of the heart,
and about this it is said:
"For the lips of the kohen shall guard knowledge,
and they shall seek Torah from his mouth,
for he is a messenger of Hashem of Hosts."
that they shall seek from his mouth:
"Rock of my heart and my portion forever."
when he entered the Kodesh HaKodashim,
was there stripped of all matter and body,
and was only a soul without a body;
and this is "the soul of man is the lamp of Hashem,"
and "One who blows, blows from within Himself"
And he was not included in "man,"
not even among those of whom it is written,
"And the likeness of their faces was the face of a man,"
for he was then greater than an angel.
And there in the Kodesh HaKodashim
לֹא הָיָה לוֹ שׁוּם דִּיבּוּר כְּלָל,
he had no speech at all,
for the prayer that he would pray
(as stated in Yoma 52b in the Mishnah).
and this too is included in
מַה שֶּׁאָמַר: הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא בִּכְבוֹדוֹ
what he said: "The Holy One, blessed be He, in His glory
For this reason the Kohen Gadol is called,
throughout the Order of the Day (in the Mishnayos of Yoma),
which derives from the word eish, fire;
for then the Kohen Gadol was
Therefore, at the last time it is mentioned
"If he found the Kohen Gadol in the marketplace,
he would say to him, 'My master, Kohen Gadol,
I have carried out your mission,'" etc. —
the Gemara's exposition of the pasuk,
"one who wishes to pour a libation of wine," etc.;
for talmidei chachamim are called ishim,
since they speak the words of the mouth of Hashem,
and the words are the "messenger of Hashem,"
which is the Holy One, blessed be He,
כְּמוֹ שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: צוּר לְבָבִי וְחֶלְקִי וְגוֹמֵר.
as it is said, "Rock of my heart and my portion," etc.
And although not every Kohen Gadol
was worthy of being stripped so completely
of all the occurrences of the body
that he would be like a soul without a body,
and nevertheless he entered the Kodesh HaKodashim —
it says in the holy sefer Avodas Yisrael
on what is said in the Gemara
"Let the descendants of the nations go in peace,
who do the deed of Aharon," etc. —
that the Kohen Gadol did not have the strength
except through the great ones of the generation,
נִכְנַס הַכֹּהֵן גָּדוֹל אָז לְקֹדֶשׁ הַקֳּדָשִׁים.
the Kohen Gadol then entered the Kodesh HaKodashim.
the great ones of the generation
and the pillars of Torah she'b'al peh;
it was through this that he was worthy
to be in the Kodesh HaKodashim,
the root of Torah she'b'al peh.
And I heard in the name of the Maggid of Kozhnitz,
may the memory of the righteous and holy one be a blessing,
that he said that then, in his time,
זֵכֶר צַדִּיק וְקָדוֹשׁ לִבְרָכָה, נִקְרָא אַבְרָהָם;
may the memory of the righteous and holy one be a blessing, is called Avraham;
the holy Rav of Lublin by the name Yitzchak;
and he himself by the name Yaakov;
that he mentioned the three Avos
based on what is said in the Midrash
בְּפַר בֶּן בָּקָר — זֶה אַבְרָהָם וְכוּלֵּי,
"'With a young bull' — this is Avraham, etc.;
'a ram for an olah' — this is Yitzchak, etc.;
'goat' — this is in the merit of Yaakov" —
meaning that the merit of the Avos entered with him.
that there were in the generation
those called by the names of the Avos,
and they could direct the kavanos
just as the great ones of the generation would direct them
the Kohen Gadol was not worthy of it.
for the kavanah to be done by another,
he said that the korbanos are not indispensable.
"There is no generation without one like Avraham,
and no generation without one like Yaakov";
and in Tanna DeVei Eliyahu Rabbah:
רַק שֶׁאֵין אָנוּ יוֹדְעִין מִי הֵם.
only we do not know who they are.
And they are able to direct
all the kavanos fitting for the Kohen Gadol.
And though we have no korbanos,
we will be able to rectify through them,
in that they will direct the intent of the korbanos
to rectify everything on Yom Kippur,
just as the Kohen Gadol would rectify
upon his entering the Kodesh HaKodashim.
